title: Executive Thesis & Prologue

epigraph.quote: Extraordinary unit economics cannot override an unverified balance sheet, an abrupt founder exit, and a broken Stage 4 tape.

web_blocks.html: Executive Verdict — REJECTED (TIER_0 | NOT_HELD | 100% CASH): NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) retains a COMPOUNDER_PASS business-quality rating with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health after delivering $115.8 billion in Q3 FY27 revenue (+103% YoY) and 74.23% ROIC [1, 2]. However, unbiased re-underwriting downgrades our new-capital verdict from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2) to REJECTED (TIER_0) on TREND, BUSINESS, and CASH_FLOW grounds. NVDA is NOT_HELD (0 shares), options are DECLINED (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE), and 100% of marginal US cash remains in USD Cash / Short-Term T-Bills.

Dual-Date Tape & Forensic Reality: On November 20, 2026, NVDA plunged -14.01% to $125.53. That close sat -39.4% below its 50D SMA ($207.00) with a 15.05 1D RSI14, tagged Stage 1 (Basing) in facts_US_2026-11-20.json [23]. On the November 23 live snapshot, shares bounced +32.5% to $166.33. Yet NVDA remains classified STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN / CAP_REJECTED) below its 50D ($206.11) and 30W ($206.95) averages. Meanwhile, Pass 1 forensics uncovered Jensen Huang's Nov 11–12 resignation, leaving CFO Colette Kress as Interim CEO [5, 29]. Long-term debt jumped 4.3x to $32.37B, and illiquid non-marketable securities hit $65.53B ($1.85B Q3 impairment) [30, 31]. Total commitments and credit guarantees reached $668B ($518B commitments, $32B neocloud, and $118.0B guarantees led by $105.0B SB Energy/OpenAI) [30]. Four direct customers drove 48% of 9M revenue, while $2.4B of Q3 China Hopper sales drop to $0 in Q4 [30, 31].

web_blocks.title: What Changes Our Mind
paragraphs: 1. An unqualified FY27 Form 10-K audit verifying $81.03B accounts receivable, $65.53B illiquid securities, and $668B commitments/guarantees alongside a permanent CEO appointment.
2. Completion of a multi-week Stage 1 base and Stage 2 breakout above rising 50-day and 30-week moving averages.

book_paragraphs: NVIDIA Corporation remains one of the most profitable technology franchises ever built, generating $215.94 billion in FY26 revenue, $96.68 billion in free cash flow, and $115.8 billion in Q3 FY27 revenue (+103% YoY). Yet great businesses are not automatically great investments at every point in their governance and market cycle. Following Pass 1 forensic verification and Round 1 Red Team stress-testing, we downgrade NVIDIA from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2) to REJECTED (TIER_0) on TREND, BUSINESS, and CASH_FLOW grounds, hold 0 shares (NOT_HELD), decline all options trades (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE), and keep 100% of marginal US capital in USD Cash and Short-Term T-Bills.

Four structural realities drive this discipline: co-founder CEO Jensen Huang's November 11–12 resignation, an active SEC accounting inquiry and California AG subpoena, a 4.3x surge in long-term debt to $32.37 billion alongside $65.53 billion in illiquid securities and $668 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees, and a broken STAGE_4 technical posture ($125.53 on November 20, -39.4% below its 50D SMA; $166.33 on November 23, CAP_REJECTED). With probability-weighted Expected Value at $163.00 and Stressed Bear at $95.00–$96.50, patience and cash preservation prevail.

This dual-date monograph reconciles both the verified November 20, 2026 session close ($125.53, -39.4% below the 50-day SMA, tagged Stage 1 in the quantitative facts ledger) and the November 23, 2026 live snapshot ($166.33, +32.5% rebound, classified STAGE_4 / CAP_REJECTED). Across both dates, the balance-sheet and governance facts remain decisive: $32.37 billion in long-term debt, $65.53 billion in illiquid non-marketable securities ($1.85 billion Q3 impairment), $81.03 billion in accounts receivable at 64 DSO, 48 percent 9M revenue concentration in four direct customers, a $2.4 billion Q3 China Hopper cliff, and $668 billion in total off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees.

In our 12-to-18-month scenario matrix, weighting a 30% Stressed Bear ($95.00, within the $95.00–$96.50 bear band), 50% Base ($175.00), and 20% Bull ($235.00) yields a probability-weighted Expected Value of $163.00—sitting 2.00 percent below the November 23 snapshot price. With our US portfolio already running at 2.34x beta and 40.3 percent correlated AI/semiconductor exposure, standing aside in USD Cash and Short-Term T-Bills is the disciplined institutional decision.
